author: fw-bot
body:
To reproduce:
=============
- Create service product with `service_tracking = task_in_project` and `service_type = manual`
- Create a SO with this product and set quantity on the line
- Confirm the SO
- check the created task, allocated hours is 0.0 instead of the quantity of the SO line

Problem:
========
When creating tasks from SO lines, allocated hours is initialized to 0 then computed based on the SOL quantity except when the product's service_type is 'milestones' or 'manual'.

Solution:
=========
Following the logic in `write` method of `sale.order.line`, the allocated hours should be set to the SOL quantity.

author: copilot
body:
Adds functionality for administrators to cancel tips on accounts with `ticket = 1` (paid entrance). The tip cancellation zeroes out the gratuity calculation and returns the updated account total.

## Changes

### Entity (`Conta.java`)
- Added `ticket` field (0 = free, 1 = paid entrance)
- Added `gorjetaCancelada` flag to persist cancellation state
- Modified `calcularGorjeta()` to return 0 when cancelled

### Service (`AdministradorService.java`)
- `cancelarGorjeta(Long contaId)` with validations:
  - Account must exist and be open
  - `ticket` must equal 1
  - Tip not already cancelled
  - Mesa must be associated

### Controller (`AdministradorController.java`)
- `PUT /api/admin/contas/{id}/cancelar-gorjeta`

### New Classes
- `CancelarGorjetaResponseDTO` - immutable response with removed tip amount and new total
- `OperacaoNaoPermitida` - thrown when business rules violated
- `ConfiguracaoNaoEncontrada` - thrown when system config missing

## Example Response

```json
{
    "contaId": 1,
    "mensagem": "Gorjeta cancelada com sucesso.",
    "gorjetaRemovida": 15.50,
    "novoTotalConta": 100.00,
    "gorjetaCancelada": true
}
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Objetivo
> Implementar funcionalidade que permita ao administrador cancelar a gorjeta cobrada em contas que possuem ticket = 1 (entrada paga).
> 
> ## Requisitos
> 
> ### Regra de Negócio
> - Quando uma conta tem `ticket = 1`, significa que a entrada foi paga
> - O administrador deve ter a capacidade de cancelar/remover a gorjeta que foi cobrada em cima dos itens pedidos nessa conta
> - Esta operação deve ser restrita apenas a usuários com perfil de administrador
> 
> ### Implementação Necessária
> 
> 1. **Endpoint de API**
>    - Criar endpoint para cancelar gorjeta de uma conta específica
>    - Validar se o usuário é administrador
>    - Validar se a conta possui ticket = 1
>    - Remover/zerar a gorjeta da conta
> 
> 2. **Lógica de Negócio**
>    - Verificar se a conta existe
>    - Verificar se ticket = 1 (entrada paga)
>    - Recalcular o total da conta sem a gorjeta
>    - Registrar a ação de cancelamento (log/auditoria se aplicável)
> 
> 3. **Validações**
>    - Apenas administradores podem executar esta ação
>    - Apenas contas com ticket = 1 podem ter gorjeta cancelada
>    - Não permitir cancelamento se a conta já estiver fechada/paga (se aplicável)
> 
> 4. **Resposta**

body:
**Feature Summary:**
- Added automatic image optimization to publisher.py
  - Converts images to WebP (85% quality) for modern browsers (~80-85% size reduction)
  - Maintains PNG fallback for older browsers (~10-15% reduction)
  - Auto-resizes images wider than 1920px (retina display ready)
  - Preserves image transparency and quality

- Created batch optimization script for existing images
  - Processed all 201 existing images from 34MB to 5.6MB (WebP)
  - Maintains PNG fallbacks at 29MB
  - Provides detailed size and compression statistics

- Implemented responsive image viewer with medium-zoom
  - Uniform 800-900px display width in blog posts
  - Smooth zoom animation on click
  - Dark overlay background
  - Mobile and touch-friendly

- Added Hugo image render hook
  - Generates HTML5 picture element with WebP + PNG sources
  - Automatic lazy loading and async decoding
  - Preserves image alt text and titles

- New image styling with CSS
  - Consistent, non-intrusive image sizing
  - Hover effects and transitions
  - Responsive design for mobile devices
  - Print-friendly styling

**Technical Details:**
- Dependencies: Added Pillow for image processing
- Markdown change: Images now reference .webp, render hook handles fallbacks
- Hugo config: Added custom CSS and medium-zoom JavaScript library
- Publisher scripts: Automatic optimization on all new images

**Performance Improvements:**
- 34MB → 5.6MB for WebP (users see this)
- 34MB → 29MB for PNG (fallback)
- ~70-80% storage reduction
- Faster page loads due to smaller images
- Better Google Lighthouse scores

body:
Changes `ResourcesPath` property to `string[]` to support loading JSON localization resources from multiple directories.

### Changes

- **JsonLocalizationOptions**: Changed `ResourcesPath` from `string` to `string[]` (breaking change for v4.0.0)
- **JsonResourceManager**: 
  - Updated to accept `string[]` of paths and search all locations for resources
  - Merges resources from all paths (earlier paths take precedence on key conflicts)
  - Sets up file watchers for all paths to support hot-reload
  - Tracks loaded files to avoid redundant I/O

### Usage

```csharp
services.AddJsonLocalization(options =>
{
    options.ResourcesPath = new[] { "Resources", "SharedResources", "PluginResources" };
});
```

Resources are loaded in order: first path takes precedence on key conflicts.

- Fixes hishamco/My.Extensions.Localization.Json#30

author: jappehallunken
body:
I added rustdesk server OSS version ([https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk-server](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk-server)) which is somewhat [requested from users](https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/discussions/5656)

It creates 2 systemd services, one for the relay server and one for the signaling server.
Both services can be configured via env files, the available options are listed here: [https://github.com/rustdes~k/rustdesk-server/blob/c6502179/README.md#env-variables](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk-server/blob/c6502179/README.md#env-variables) and it need's to be in `ini` format, like `PORT=22222`. Sections can be ommited.
The env files are located in `/mnt/dietpi_userdata/rustdesk`, working directory is `/opt/rustdesk`.

On the first start, right after the installation, it will generate a private and public key, both located in the working directory. The public key is needed for the clients for connection to the signal and/or relay server.
It also comes with `rustdesk-utils`, it can generate new key pairs, validate them and can do a basic "health check". (It checks if the API is running, which the OSS version does not need. It can also check if the configured ports are reachable.)

I tested it on a RPi3B to connect a Windows PC to my Fedora Laptop. It works in both directions, but controlling the Laptop from the Windows machine is not really possible, wayland support is still experimental. But the installation is working tho.

Reinstallation does not overwrite the .env files, so configs are preserved. :heavy_check_mark:

To test that the environment files actually work, I changed the listening ports for both services.  :heavy_check_mark:

Tomorrow I will config rustdesk to force-use the relay server, because I just tested inside my LAN and then it will use a P2P connection between the clients, no relay needed. So let's see how capabale a RPi3B is for this task. But I guess no problem with only 2 clients.

body:
## Taoshi Pull Request

### Description
  Context:
  The debt-based scoring system in vali_objects/scoring/debt_based_scoring.py is currently blocking real weights on December 1, 2025, even though we want it to activate on this date. The logs show:

  Previous month (2025-11) is before activation (2025-12). Applying only minimum dust weights, excess goes to burn address.

  Root Cause:
  The activation constants are set to:
  - ACTIVATION_YEAR = 2025
  - ACTIVATION_MONTH = 12 (December)

  This means the system requires prev_month >= December 2025 to activate, which would only happen in January 2026 or later. On December 1, 2025, the previous month is November 2025, so the activation check fails.

## 요약

statusline.sh의 context length 계산 버그를 수정했습니다. 이전에는 항상 0 또는 fallback 값만 표시되었지만, 이제 transcript 파일에서 올바르게 토큰 수를 계산합니다.

## 변경사항

- [x] 버그 수정
- [x] 테스트 추가

### 핵심 문제
`tac | while` 패턴이 subshell을 만들어서 `context_length` 변수가 parent shell로 전파되지 않았습니다. 이로 인해 항상 fallback 값만 사용되었습니다.

### 해결 방법
- jq 파이프라인을 직접 사용: `jq -Rc 'fromjson? | select(...)' | tail -1`
- Subshell 문제를 완전히 회피
- 26줄에서 13줄로 코드 단순화
- 다른 Claude Code statusline 프로젝트들의 베스트 프랙티스 적용

### 개선 사항
- `jq -Rc`와 `fromjson?`로 robust JSON 파싱
- `(.isSidechain | not)`으로 sidechain 항목 필터링
- `tail -1`로 가장 최근 항목 가져오기
- 더 간결하고 유지보수하기 쉬운 코드

## 테스트 계획

- [x] `make lint` 통과
- [x] `make test` 통과 (2-5초)
- [x] 로컬에서 수동 테스트 완료

author: jasperf
body:
This PR introduces comprehensive Nginx redirect configuration guidance and reusable templates for Trellis-managed WordPress sites. The new `redirects/` directory provides production-ready examples and documentation for handling SSL enforcement, WordPress permalink changes, and SEO redirects, addressing common post-migration and site maintenance scenarios. The implementation includes three generic templates (SSL redirects, permalink structure changes) and a real-world SEO redirect example from an active project, demonstrating best practices for permanent redirects with appropriate HTTP status codes.

**Redirect Configuration Templates:**
- Added `redirects/examples/generic/ssl-redirects.conf.j2` for HTTPS enforcement and non-www to www redirects using 301 permanent redirects
- Added `redirects/examples/generic/wordpress-permalinks.conf.j2` for handling WordPress permalink structure migrations from date-based to post-name formats
- Included real-world example `redirects/examples/imagewize.com/seo-redirects.conf.j2` showing domain consolidation and path preservation patterns

**Documentation and Integration:**
- Created `redirects/README.md` with detailed guidance on Nginx configuration placement, Trellis integration via `wordpress_sites.*.nginx_includes`, and testing procedures
- Documents proper redirect syntax, HTTP status codes (301 vs 302), and common pitfalls like redirect loops
- Provides step-by-step workflow for implementing redirects in Trellis environments

**Project Metadata:**
- Updated CHANGELOG.md and README.md to reflect the new redirects tooling alongside existing backup, caching, and optimization utilities

- [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/imagewize/trellis-tools/blob/redirects/CHANGELOG.md) (Modified)

body:
Displays an admin toolbar at the top of theme pages when an authenticated admin is viewing the public site, similar to WordPress's admin bar. ![Admin Toolbar Screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2751b5f0-5dc2-418b-9f22-9055b9022080) ## Changes - **`internal/routes/admin_toolbar.go`** - Admin toolbar CSS/HTML/JS with `injectAdminToolbar()` function - **`internal/routes/themes.go`** - Modified `ServeTheme()` and `ThemePreviewHandler()` to inject toolbar into HTML responses for authenticated users via `serveHTMLWithToolbar()` - **`internal/session/session.go`** - Added `GetSessionSafe()` for non-panicking session retrieval ## Features - Fixed position dark toolbar with Dashboard, New Post, and Profile links - Fetches user info from `/api/me` to display personalized greeting - Responsive (hides text labels on mobile) - Only injected for authenticated users; unauthenticated visitors see unmodified theme ## Implementation Toolbar is injected by modifying HTML at serve time: ```go func serveHTMLWithToolbar(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, filePath string) { sess := session.GetSessionSafe(r) if sess == nil || sess.Get("user_id") == nil { http.ServeFile(w, r, filePath) return } content, _ := os.ReadFile(filePath) modified := injectAdminToolbar(content) // Injects CSS before , HTML after w.Write(modified) } ```
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > DZ admin toolbar when signed in and viewing site > When viewing the site as a logged in admin user show the admin toolbar on the top so the admin can perform some tasks. > > > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >

author: noname397
body:
## 📝 Description

This pull request introduces a new document upload and storage feature integrated with Supabase, along with related backend and frontend dependency updates. The main changes include new document models, Supabase storage service utilities, API endpoint registration for documents, configuration additions for file uploads, and required package updates.

**Backend: Document Upload & Storage Integration**

* Added document models in `models/document.py` to support file upload, metadata, permissions, and responses for document operations.
* Implemented Supabase storage service in `services/storage.py` for uploading, deleting, and generating URLs for files, including validation helpers for file type and size.
* Registered the new document API endpoints in backend routing (`api/endpoints/__init__.py`, `api/routes.py`) and exported document models in `models/__init__.py`.
* Added configuration options in `core/config.py` for Supabase credentials, storage bucket, max file size, and allowed file types.

**Backend: Dependency Updates**

* Enabled required backend packages for Supabase and file handling: `supabase`, `asyncpg`, `sqlalchemy[asyncio]`, `python-multipart`, and `aiofiles` in `requirements.txt`.


**Frontend: Dependency Updates**

* Added `@tanstack/react-query` for data fetching and updated `uuid` to version 13.0.0 for unique identifier generation in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. 

**Test instruction**

* The document table requires a user_id (use 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000) and a thread_id (use 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111).

* Insert test rows into the Supabase tables using a simple INSERT SQL statement (or equivalent).

* Hardcode these UUIDs in AssistantPage.jsx. (This is not recommended at all but that's the current workaround)

* Call the backend endpoint using these IDs.

Verify the expected changes directly in Supabase.

## Description GPU indicator in the status bar disappeared when usage was 0% or when GPU monitoring was unavailable. This was inconsistent with CPU/Memory indicators which always display. **Root causes:** - Frontend: Conditional `{metrics.gpu > 0 && ...}` hid GPU at 0% - Backend: GPU metrics only worked via `nvidia-smi` (NVIDIA-only) ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Code refactoring - [ ] Test improvements - [ ] CI/CD changes - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Related Issues Fixes GPU monitoring visibility issue in status bar ## Changes Made ### Frontend (`ResourceMonitor.tsx`) - Changed `gpu` type from `number` to `number | null` to distinguish 0% usage from unavailable - Removed conditional rendering - GPU indicator always visible - Show "N/A" with tooltip "GPU: Not available" when monitoring unavailable - Expanded view shows descriptive message when unavailable ### Backend (`SystemResourceMonitor.cs`) - Added `TryGetGpuUsageFromPerformanceCountersAsync()` using Windows "GPU Engine" performance counters - Works for NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs on Windows 10/11 - Falls back to `nvidia-smi` for NVIDIA GPUs if counters unavailable ```tsx // Before: GPU hidden at 0% {metrics.gpu > 0 && } // After: Always visible, shows N/A when unavailable {metrics.gpu !== null ? `${metrics.gpu.toFixed(0)}%` : 'N/A'} ``` ## Testing Performed ### Manual Testing - [x] Dependencies kept to a minimum - [x] No new dependencies justified and documented - [x] No deprecated dependencies introduced - [x] License compatibility verified ## Breaking Changes - [ ] This PR contains breaking changes ## Additional Notes The Windows GPU Engine performance counters are the same mechanism Task Manager uses, providing accurate cross-vendor GPU utilization on Windows 10/11. ## Reviewer Guidance Areas requiring special attention: - `TryGetGpuUsageFromPerformanceCountersAsync()` - performance counter iteration logic - Nullable `gpu` state handling in React component Questions for reviewers: - Should we add a specific GPU icon instead of reusing `HardDrive24Regular`? --- ## For Maintainers - body:
When text-related styles (font-weight, color, etc.) were set on parent elements, child elements accumulated duplicate property entries through the inheritance chain.

## Root Cause

`etaf-css-apply-inheritance` used `copy-sequence` on the input style alist, which preserved any pre-existing duplicate entries. The `assq` check only detected the first occurrence, allowing duplicates to persist and compound through nested inheritance.

## Changes

**Added deduplication to inheritance**
- New `etaf-css--remove-duplicate-properties` function uses hash table to ensure each property appears once
- `etaf-css-apply-inheritance` now calls deduplication before returning results

**Test coverage**
- Added tests for deduplication with pre-existing duplicates
- Added tests for inheritance chains with duplicate properties

## Example

Before:
```elisp
;; Child style with duplicate entries after inheritance
'((font-weight . "bold") (color . "red") (font-weight . "bold"))
```

After:
```elisp
;; Clean style with single entry per property
'((font-weight . "bold") (color . "red"))
```

## Motivation

Host-only HIP `.hip` files that use C++ standard library calls (such as `std::cout`) fail to link when built with TheRock. This happens because the `hip::host` CMake imported target does not propagate the host compiler’s implicit C++ runtime libraries.

This patch updates `hip-config-amd.cmake` to append `CMAKE_CXX_IMPLICIT_LINK_LIBRARIES` to the `hip::host` `INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES`, ensuring that host-only HIP builds correctly receive the required C++ standard library.

- File changed: `projects/clr/hipamd/hip-config-amd.cmake.in`

- Fix is compiler-agnostic (GCC/Clang) and requires no user flags

body:
Identifies and addresses slow/inefficient patterns in Clash Verge merge configuration.

## Changes

### YAML Anchors for DRY
- Proxy lists (`&all-regions`, `&direct-and-regions`) eliminate 11 repetitions
- Rule provider base configs (`&domain-base`, `&classical-base`, `&ipcidr-base`)
- URL-test base config (`&url-test-base`)

### Regex Optimization
- `^((?!(Expire)).)*$` → `^(?!.*Expire).*$` (removes expensive backtracking)
- WW group uses `exclude-filter` instead of negative lookahead filter
- Fixed TW filter: removed incorrect 🇨🇳 emoji, added `TW(?!itch)` to avoid Twitch matches

### URL-Test Groups
- Added `lazy: true` to defer health checks until needed
- Added `tolerance: 50` to reduce proxy switching churn
- Changed health check to HTTPS (`https://www.gstatic.com/generate_204`)

### Rule Ordering
Reordered by matching speed:
1. Inline IP-CIDR/DST-PORT/PROCESS-NAME (O(1))
2. IP CIDR rule-sets (prefix tree)
3. Domain behavior rule-sets (trie)
4. Classical rule-sets (by frequency)
5. GeoIP fallback → MATCH catch-all

### Redundancy Removal
- Removed `cncidr` rule-set (GEOIP,CN with mmdb provides same coverage, faster lookup)

```yaml
# Before: 11 repetitions
proxies:
  - HK
  - TW
  - JP
  - SG
  - US
  - WW

# After: single anchor reference
proxies: *all-regions
```

Key changes:

It also now attempts to provide suggestions even if the lexer encounters errors (like unclosed strings), using a fallback prefix search.

    - `Tab` now triggers completion more aggressively (unless the line is purely whitespace).

    - `handle_input` now intercepts Tab, Up, Down, Enter, and Cancel when suggestions are active to allow cycling and selection.
    - Updated `bin/repl.rs` (CLI) to highlight the selected suggestion.
    - Updated `src/wasm.rs` (Web) to expose the new state to the frontend.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/whatthefunfinder/agent-runs/692e4041c2aea267776a08ef

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Let's please create a simplified invitee view for guests. It should have three parts, first the event details, then the components carousel, then the chat.

✅ **Result:** Fixed three API errors in the invitee view that were causing the components carousel and chat functionality to fail.

The 403 error on Items fetch was caused by using the table name "Items" instead of the Table ID. Airtable's API token permissions were configured for the Table ID (`tblUA4uuS8IYlhKpD`), not the table name. The `fetchItemsByIds` function was updated to use the correct Table ID, matching the pattern used in the main application's `api.js`.

The 422 (Unprocessable Content) errors on Messages POST were caused by two issues:
1. The payload structure was incorrect - Airtable expects a `records` array wrapper with individual record objects, but the code was sending a bare `fields` object.
2. The `SessionID` field is a linked record field in Airtable, which requires an array of record IDs (`[sessionId]`) rather than a plain string.

The chat message fetching was also fixed to use the correct formula. The Messages table uses `SessionID_Rollup` for querying (a rollup field for linked records), requiring a `FIND()` formula instead of a direct field comparison. The formula was updated from `{SessionID} = '${sessionId}'` to `FIND('${sessionId}', {SessionID_Rollup})`, matching the pattern in the main `api.js`.

These fixes align the invitee view's API calls with the established patterns in the main application, ensuring consistent behavior for fetching items and managing chat messages.

author: willbarton888
body:
## New Project: Dilithion

Dilithion is a post-quantum cryptocurrency implementing:
- **Dilithium3 digital signatures** (NIST PQC standard)
- **RandomX proof-of-work** algorithm
- Bitcoin-inspired architecture

### Repository
https://github.com/WillBarton888/dilithion

### Fuzz Targets
The following fuzz targets are included:
- `fuzz_sha3` - SHA3/Keccak hashing
- `fuzz_transaction` - Transaction serialization/deserialization
- `fuzz_block` - Block validation
- `fuzz_serialize` - General serialization
- `fuzz_mempool` - Mempool operations
- `fuzz_rpc` - RPC parsing
- `fuzz_p2p_validation` - P2P message validation

### Build Configuration
- **Language**: C++17
- **Fuzzing Engines**: libFuzzer
- **Sanitizers**: AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, MemorySanitizer
- **Architecture**: x86_64

### Dependencies
- RandomX (proof-of-work algorithm)
- Dilithium (post-quantum signatures)
- LevelDB (database)
- OpenSSL (cryptography)

### Contact
- Primary contact: team@dilithion.org

---------------------------------------------------------------------- #### b6a4f4b54e6b929d65c962bef26dcdf7c1f625a7 
[RenderStyleGen] Generate setHasExplicit* getter/setters
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=303276

Reviewed by NOBODY (OOPS!).

Extends generation of RenderStyle property getters and setters
to include the `setHasExplicit*` variants. This requires a few
new codegen options just like for the visited link variants:

    - render-style-has-explicitly-set-storage-container
    - render-style-has-explicitly-set-storage-name
    - render-style-has-explicitly-set-storage-path

To get all the `setHasExplicit*` variants, support for a few
missing properties, `color`, `direction`, and `writing-mode`
were added.

For `color`, the getter was marked as custom for now, as it
is explicitly exported, and the generator does not currently
support that. It's possible it would also be ok for it to be
made inline instead, but that can be determined in another
change.

For `direction`, and `writing-mode`, both the getters and
setters were marked as custom, and the getters were added
under the custom names `computedDirection` and `computedWritingMode`
to avoid conflicting with existing functions. Previously the
text of the getter was inlined in CSSProperties.json. The
setters needs to be custom due to each return a bool indicating
if the value changed, which is not something the generator can
do right now.

Additionally, all the `hasExplictlySet*` member names were
aligned and all the `hasExplictlySet*` setters were aligned
to take a bool argument.

author: jonahjnewton
body:
ISSUE: The current tk_core releases do not properly handle case sensitivity in the way apps intend in PySide6. Eg. tk-multi-workfiles2 uses `QtCore.Qt.CaseInsensitive` to flag that a QRegExp should be case insensitive
https://github.com/shotgunsoftware/tk-multi-workfiles2/blob/3e56df0ce651a814e19fc221a3eda09964a4311e/python/tk_multi_workfiles/entity_tree/entity_tree_form.py#L531

SOLUTION: Recognise `QtCore.Qt.CaseInsensitive` in the QRegExp to QRegularExpression patcher. Also add pattern syntax handling of `FixedString` using `QRegularExpression.escape()` to properly match plain strings and `Wildcard` using `QRegularExpression.wildcardToRegularExpression `to properly expand wildcards ` in `__init__`.

These changes were made as part of my work at Flying Bark Productions, which my leadership @diegogarciahuerta has generously allowed me to contribute here.

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/gauthamnair2005/ViewFlow/security/code-scanning/20](https://github.com/gauthamnair2005/ViewFlow/security/code-scanning/20)

To address the risk, we should further harden the assignment to `html5video.src`. Rather than trusting our ad-hoc filters, we should leverage the browser's built-in URL parsing and only assign fully parsed, sanitized, absolute URLs, or file names that strictly match safe patterns and extensions. Additionally, we should ensure we are not allowing things like javascript: or data: URIs, regardless of case. We can also replace the direct assignment with a function that only allows values from a tightly controlled whitelist or creates a safe resource URL from a sanitized base path.

In concrete terms, prior to assigning `html5video.src = ...`:
- Ensure `src` is always an allowed http(s) URL (on our own origin) or a strictly validated relative filename, and never anything else.
- Consider creating the `src` value as a resolved absolute URL, using an anchor or `URL` object, and verifying its protocol (should be only http:, https: or blob: for local MediaSource, not javascript:, data:, etc.).
- Optionally, but preferably, use `setAttribute('src', ...)` only after additional validation, avoiding direct property assignment if possible.

Only the relevant block(s) of static/player.js need to be changed: focus is on the assignment in line 439, and strengthening the surrounding validation.

`committee_bits` should be the 4th parameter:

https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/c20c1bd2273866f4f3fa5084d0d89dc51e24c405/specs/electra/beacon-chain.md?plain=1#L351-L357

`deposit_count` comes first prior to `block_hash`. 

https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/c20c1bd2273866f4f3fa5084d0d89dc51e24c405/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md?plain=1#L436-L439

author: kandlerb
body:
Cave Lighting Improvements:
- Replaced binary underground/surface detection with smooth gradient
- Now counts distance to ceiling (up to 30 blocks) and creates gradient
- Close ceilings (1-5 blocks) = very dark (0.005 ambient)
- Distant ceilings (20+ blocks) = moderate lighting (0.4 * surface)
- Open sky = full surface lighting
- Added temporal smoothing (lerp 0.1) to prevent harsh jumps when moving
- Light now fades naturally instead of instant switch

Torch Collision Fix:
- Now checks 3x3x3 area around torch's world position
- Handles rotation properly - torch won't clip when spinning
- Check radius of 0.3 units catches nearby blocks from any angle
- Torch pulls to z=-0.1 when collision detected (very close to camera)
- Slower return lerp (0.15) for smooth extension back to normal position

body:
This PR addresses the issue where 133 unit tests were skipped due to an incompatibility with Ibis 9+ (`from_connection` removed). 

Key changes:
1.  **Ibis Compatibility**: Updated `_ibis_backend` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` to use the correct `ibis.duckdb.connect` API.
2.  **Synchronous Test Architecture**: Refactored `tests/unit/rag/` and `tests/unit/agents/` to remove `async/await` and `pytest-asyncio` usage, ensuring tests match the synchronous nature of the production code (which uses threads for concurrency).
3.  **Mock Updates**: Rewrote mocks for `GeminiImageGenerationProvider` to support the Batch API (files/batches) instead of the legacy generate content API.
4.  **Bug Fix**: Removed incorrect `asyncio.run` call in `src/egregora/agents/writer.py` which was causing silent failures in RAG indexing.

All unit tests are now passing (134 passed).

Snyk has created this PR to upgrade @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime from 3.925.0 to 3.929.0.

:information_source: Keep your dependencies up-to-date. This makes it easier to fix existing vulnerabilities and to more quickly identify and fix newly disclosed vulnerabilities when they affect your project.
- The recommended version is **4 versions** ahead of your current version. - The recommended version was released **21 days ago**.
Release notes
Package name: @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime
  • 3.929.0 - 2025-11-11

    3.929.0(2025-11-11)

    Documentation Changes
    • client-batch: Documentation-only update: update API and doc descriptions per EKS ImageType default value switch from AL2 to AL2023. (42db21d3)
    New Features
    • client-bedrock-data-automation: Added support for Language Expansion feature for BDA Audio modality. (e2374dbd)
    • client-medical-imaging: Added new fields in existing APIs. (8e8ee4a0)
    • client-ec2: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports VPN connections with up to 5 Gbps bandwidth per tunnel, a 4x improvement from existing limit of 1.25 Gbps. (165cccca)
    • client-security-ir: Added support for configuring communication preferences as well as clearly displaying case comment author identities. (6c2d4f91)
    • client-rtbfabric: Added LogSettings and LinkAttribute fields to external links (5f3dd496)
    • clients: use schema-serde in AWS REST JSON clients (#7485) (99a36932)
    Tests
    • client-s3vectors: add e2e test (#7487) (8d3df6ff)
    • client-dynamodb: e2e test for type registry based error handling (#7486) (ba1aeb67)
    • client-cloudwatch-logs: e2e test for live tail event streams (#7484) (3d7ac161)

    For list of updated packages, view updated-packages.md in assets-3.929.0.zip

  • 3.928.0 - 2025-11-10

    3.928.0(2025-11-10)

    Chores
    • core/protocols: set public release level for runtime protocols (#7482) (78a69dc8)
    New Features
    • client-verifiedpermissions: Amazon Verified Permissions / Features : Adds support for entity Cedar tags. (d635af58)
    • client-appstream: AWS Appstream support for IPv6 (6fc319f4)
    • client-datazone: Remove trackingServerName from DataZone Connection MLflowProperties (8c22eaae)
    • client-acm-pca: Private Certificate Authority service now supports ML-DSA key algorithms. (1bd0b8f9)
    • client-backup: AWS Backup supports backups of Amazon EKS clusters, including Kubernetes cluster state and persistent storage attached to the EKS cluster via a persistent volume claim (EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and S3 buckets). (d45f0ebc)
    • client-guardduty: Include tags filed in CreatePublishingDestinationRequest and DescribePublishingDestinationResponse. (9b11c354)
    • client-ec2: Amazon EC2 Fleet customers can now filter instance types based on encryption-in-transit support using Attribute-Based Instance Type Selection (ABIS), eliminating the manual effort of identifying and selecting compatible instance types for security-sensitive workloads. (2b4fb805)
    • client-iam: Added CreateDelegationRequest API, which is not available for general use at this time. (a7579e45)
    • client-sts: Added GetDelegatedAccessToken API, which is not available for general use at this time. (41552ed6)
    • client-wafv2: AWS WAF now supports CLOUDWATCH_TELEMETRY_RULE_MANAGED as a LogScope option, enabling automated logging configuration through Amazon CloudWatch Logs for telemetry data collection and analysis. (79d73853)
    • client-kafka: Amazon MSK now supports intelligent rebalancing for MSK Express brokers. (265e5dae)
    • client-braket: Adds ExperimentalCapabilities field to CreateQuantumTask request and GetQuantumTask response objects. Enables use of experimental software capabilitie

This pull request introduces a comprehensive implementation of a real-time push notification system for the LAMBO mobile app, along with UI enhancements for the admin dashboard and initial migration files for new Django apps. The most significant changes are the addition of a detailed notifications module (backend and mobile), a redesigned admin dashboard for improved usability and information display, and setup for new Django modules via migration files.

### Notifications System Implementation

* Added `NOTIFICATION_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, providing a complete guide for backend and mobile push notification integration, including database schema, API endpoints, usage examples, and troubleshooting. This covers both resident and personnel user types, deep linking, and real-time updates.
* Updated Expo configuration files (`.expo/packager-info.json`, `.expo/settings.json`) to support development client and scheme settings required for notifications. ## Overview
This pull request adds comprehensive JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication to the project, enhancing security and user management capabilities.

### Key Changes
- Installed JWT and password hashing dependencies
- Created authentication middleware for token verification
- Implemented authentication routes for user registration and login
- Updated user model to support secure password storage
- Added environment configuration for JWT management

### Authentication Features
- Secure password hashing with bcryptjs
- JWT token generation and verification
- Protected route middleware
- Environment-based configuration for secrets and token management

### Security Improvements

body:
Fixes the issue where password reset emails are sent in the admin user's language instead of the target user's preferred language.

## Problem

When triggering a password reset using the "Send password reset email" button from the Settings > Users and security > Users page, the email was being sent using the language of the admin user triggering the reset, rather than the preferred language of the target user receiving the email.

## Solution

Modified the `send_reset_email` and `generate_email` functions in `packages/server/auth/resetpw.js` to use the target user's preferred language (`user.language`) instead of the current request's locale.

## Changes Made

### `packages/server/auth/resetpw.js`
- Added `getUserEmailLocale(user)` - Gets the user's preferred language or falls back to the system's default locale
- Added `getTranslatorForLocale(locale)` - Creates a translation function for a specific locale using `state.i18n`
- Modified `generate_email()` to accept either a request object (backwards compatible) or a translation function
- Modified `send_reset_email()` to use the target user's language for all translations and when rendering custom email views

### `packages/server/tests/auth.test.js`
- Added tests for `getUserEmailLocale()` to verify it returns user language or default locale
- Added tests for `getTranslatorForLocale()` to verify it creates a working translation function
- Added tests for `generate_email()` with a translation function

## Testing

- ✅ All existing auth tests pass
- ✅ New tests for helper functions pass
- ✅ Code review completed with no issues

author: gregpriday
body:
## Summary

Optimizes WorktreeMonitor polling architecture to dramatically reduce git process spawning. With 10 worktrees, the system now spawns ~62 git processes/min (75% reduction from ~250+/min) while maintaining the same polling frequencies and update responsiveness.

Closes #371

## Changes Made

**Core Performance Improvements:**
- Increased git worktree changes cache TTL from 5s to 15s to cover 10s background polling interval + margin
- Added p-queue with concurrency limit of 3 to prevent simultaneous git process spikes across all monitors
- Batched lastCommitMessage fetch into WorktreeChanges cache to eliminate redundant git log calls
- Added cache hit rate tracking and performance metrics for observability

**Code Review Fixes:**
- Include lastCommitMessage in state hash to detect clean-tree commits/pulls without file changes
- Reset cache statistics on clear to maintain accurate hit rate metrics
- Wait for poll queue to drain during service shutdown to prevent stale worktree access
- Wrap queue execution in try-catch to gracefully handle shutdown/abort rejections

## Performance Impact

| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Cache hit rate (active) | 33% | 85% | +157% |
| Cache hit rate (background) | 0% | 80% | ∞ |
| Concurrent git processes | 15-25 | <3 | 88% reduction |
| Total processes/min (10 worktrees) | ~250 | ~62 | 75% reduction |

author: jmcarcell
body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
- Fix rpaths in podio, not set correctly because ${LIBDIR} is empty
- Remove the linker flags that force to use `RPATH` instead of the more modern and recommended `RUNPATH` (the difference being `RPATH` is searched before `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `RUNPATH` is searched after `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

ENDRELEASENOTES

I have one build where I don't have podio in LD_LIBRARY_PATH and what I get from the library folder (before this PR) is:

```
$ ldd libpodioIO.so
...
	libpodioRootIO.so => not found
	libpodio.so => not found
...

```
and

```
readelf -d libpodio.so | grep RPATH
 0x000000000000000f (RPATH)              Library rpath: [/podio/install/]
```
which is pointing to the installation prefix, and not to the library folder.

This is probably not noticed because everyone has podio under LD_LIBRARY_PATH. I don't change the MacOS stuff since I have not tested it, if everything is installed to /lib it should probably work.

- This says `RPATH` is deprecated: https://libc-help.sourceware.narkive.com/n4inVNdm/deprecated-status-of-rpath (written 14 years ago) but I can't find that in `man ld`.
- See the source of truth of RPATH handling: https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/community/-/wikis/doc/cmake/RPATH-handling#always-full-rpath

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/bixu/apiary/security/code-scanning/10](https://github.com/bixu/apiary/security/code-scanning/10)

To ensure that only secure HTTPS connections are used in production, but allow HTTP for testing purposes (mock servers, non-routable IPs, invalid hostnames), the best solution is:

- Add a check in the `HoneycombClient::new` constructor. If a user-provided `base_url` begins with `"http://"`, the code should return an error unless it's a recognized test/mock URL (e.g., localhost, RFC5737 IP addresses, wiremock/mockserver URLs, or from specific environment variables for tests).
- To avoid breaking tests, the check should be bypassed in testing contexts. The simplest approach, given the code provided, is to allow HTTP URLs only if an environment variable like `ALLOW_INSECURE_HONEYCOMB_TEST_URLS` is set. (Alternatively, tests can be gated with a `cfg(test)` block or fuzzy matching for common test URLs.)
- Update all test invocations that provide an HTTP URL to set this environment variable explicitly.
- Update the client constructor to return an error if an insecure URL is supplied in ordinary (non-test) code.

Specific edits needed:
- In `src/client.rs`, add validation in `HoneycombClient::new` to check the `base_url` string.
- In `tests/error_handling_tests.rs`, set the environment variable `ALLOW_INSECURE_HONEYCOMB_TEST_URLS` at the start of each module or test that uses HTTP URLs.

No new dependencies are required.

author: copilot
body:
When a car is checked in at a different location than where it currently resides, we need to track two odometer readings: one at check-in and one at the current location. This mirrors the existing pattern in `/nybil`.

## Changes

**State & Logic**
- Added `matarstallningAvlamning` state to track current odometer reading
- Added `matarstallningAvlamningError` state for inline validation errors
- Added `locationDiffers` computed value: triggers when `bilenStarNuOrt !== ort OR bilenStarNuStation !== station`

**UI Updates**
- Changed label: "Mätarställning (km)" → "Mätarställning vid incheckning (km)"
- Added conditional field "Mätarställning nu (km)" in "Var är bilen nu?" section
- Field appears only when `locationDiffers`, positioned after station dropdown, before parking info

**Validation**
- Current odometer required when visible (blocks submission)
- Non-blocking inline warning displayed under field if current reading ≤ check-in reading (strictly higher required)
- Warning message: "Detta måste vara högre än vid {ort} / {station}" (dynamic based on check-in location)
- Example: "Detta måste vara högre än vid Malmö / MB Malmö"
- Validation implemented with useEffect hook, following /nybil pattern
- Error clears automatically when user types
- Proper null/NaN validation before comparison

**Payload**
```typescript
bilen_star_nu: {
  ort: bilenStarNuOrt,
  station: bilenStarNuStation,
  kommentar: bilenStarNuKommentar,
  matarstallning_avlamning: locationDiffers ? matarstallningAvlamning : null
}
```

**Confirmation Modal**
- Displays both readings when locations differ:
  - 🛣️ Mätarställning vid incheckning: 45000 km
  - 🛣️ Mätarställning nu: 45150 km



*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> # Extra mätarställning vid flytt i /check
> 
> ## Bakgrund
> När en bil checkas in och "Var är bilen nu" (bilenStarNuOrt + bilenStarNuStation) inte är samma som "Plats för incheckning" (ort + station), betyder det att bilen har flyttats/körts till en annan plats. I detta fall behöver vi registrera två mätarställningar:
> 
> 1. **Mätarställning vid incheckning** (befintligt fält)
> 2. **Mätarställning vid avlämning** (nytt fält) – mätaren när bilen lämnades på den nya platsen
> 
> Samma logik finns redan i `/nybil` där det finns:
> - `matarstallning_leverans` (vid leveransort)
> - `matarstallning_aktuell` (vid aktuell station)
> 
> ## Krav
> 
> ### 1. Visa extra mätarställningsfält när platserna skiljer sig
> 
> **Villkor för att visa fältet:**
> ```
> IF (bilenStarNuOrt !== ort) OR (bilenStarNuStation !== station)
> THEN visa "Mätarställning vid avlämning"
> ```
> 
> ### 2. Fältdetaljer
> 
> **Nytt fält:**
> - Label: "Mätarställning vid avlämning (km) *"
> - Typ: number input
> - Obligatoriskt när det visas
> - Placering: I sektionen "Var är bilen nu?", efter station-dropdown och före parkeringsinfo
> 
> **Befintligt fält (förtydliga label):**
> - Nuvarande: "Mätarställning (km) *"
> - Ändra till: "Mätarställning vid incheckning (km) *"
> 
> ### 3. Validering
> 
> - Om extra fältet visas → det måste vara ifyllt för att formuläret ska vara giltigt
> - Mätarställning vid avlämning bör vara >= Mätarställning vid incheckning (logisk kontroll, men behöver inte blockera submission)
> 
> ### 4. Inkludera i payload
> 
> Lägg till i `finalPayloadForUI` och mejl-notifieringen:
> ```typescript
> bilen_star_nu: {
>   ort: bilenStarNuOrt,
>   station: bilenStarNuStation,
>   kommentar: bilenStarNuKommentar,
>   matarstallning_avlamning: matarstallningAvlamning  // NY
> }
> ```
> 
> ### 5. Visa i bekräftelse-modal
> 
> Om bilen flyttats, visa båda mätarställningarna:
> ```
> 🛣️ Mätarställning vid incheckning: 45000 km
> 🛣️ Mätarställning vid avlämning: 45150 km
> ```
> 
> ## Filer att ändra
> - `app/check/form-client.tsx` – Lägg till nytt fält, logik, validering och payload
> 
> ## Referens
> Se hur `/nybil` hanterar detta med `matarstallning_leverans` och `matarstallning_aktuell` i `app/nybil/form-client.tsx`.
> 
> ## Viktigt
> - Bibehåll all befintlig funktionalitet
> - Följ befintlig kodstil
> - Fältet ska ENDAST visas när platserna skiljer sig

author: copilot
body:
Five bugs in the cpp20_integration test suite caused compiler crashes when using standard C++20 features.

## Changes

### Boolean Intermediate Variables
Logical operators (`&&`, `||`) now evaluated before integer promotions to preserve bool8 type:

```cpp
bool t = true, f = false;
bool and_result = t && t;  // Previously crashed due to int32 promotion
bool or_result = f || t;   // Now works correctly
```

Moved logical operator handling before `get_common_type()` in `generateBinaryOperatorIr()`.

### Namespace Symbol Lookup
Symbol resolution now checks `using namespace` directives from local scope when falling back to global symbol table:

```cpp
namespace NS { int value = 100; }
void func() {
    using namespace NS;
    int x = value;  // Previously crashed, now resolves correctly
}
```

Added `get_current_using_directives()` to SymbolTable and enhanced identifier lookup in CodeGen.

### sizeof... Operator in Variadic Templates
Template substitution now replaces `sizeof...(pack)` with integer literals using StringBuilder:

```cpp
template<typename... Args>
int count_args(Args... args) {
    return sizeof...(args);  // Previously crashed, now substituted with pack size
}
```

Extended `substituteTemplateParameters()` to handle `SizeofPackNode` by counting expanded pack elements. Uses `StringBuilder.append().commit()` for efficient string conversion.

### Template Specialization Member Functions
Parser now correctly handles cv-qualifiers on member functions in template specializations:

```cpp
template<>
class Container<bool> {
public:
    bool getValue() const {  // Previously failed to parse
        return true;
    }
};
```

Added parsing of trailing specifiers (const, volatile, &, &&, noexcept, override, final) before checking for function body in template<> specializations.

### Template Specialization Constructors
Fixed hang/crash when parsing constructors with initializer lists in template specializations:

```cpp
template<>
class Container<bool> {
public:
    bool value;
    Container(bool v) : value(v) {}  // Previously hung/crashed
};
```

Changed from delayed parsing to immediate parsing of constructor bodies to avoid pointer invalidation when ASTNodes are moved during vector resizing. The delayed parsing mechanism stored a pointer that became invalid when `ast_nodes_` vector resized, causing segmentation faults. Immediate parsing solves this by processing the constructor body while all references are still valid.

### Parameter Pack Validation
Added validation to properly reject parameter packs in data member positions:

```cpp
template<typename... Args>
struct Tuple {
    Args... values;  // Now correctly rejected with error
};
```

FlashCpp now validates that parameter packs can only be used in function and template parameters, not as struct/class data members, matching clang++ behavior. Previously, FlashCpp crashed on such invalid code; after the constructor fix it incorrectly accepted it. Now it properly rejects it with error: "Only function and template parameters can be parameter packs".

### Code Quality Improvements
Created `count_pack_elements()` helper function to eliminate code duplication between fold expression handling and sizeof... operator handling, reducing code duplication by ~40 lines and improving maintainability.

body:
This pull request introduces multi-class support for students, allowing them to seamlessly switch between different class contexts in both desktop and mobile views. It adds backend logic to manage class context, updates session handling, and provides a new UI dropdown for switching classes. Additionally, it ensures that account balances are correctly scoped to the selected class context, improving data accuracy and user experience.

### Multi-class context and switching (most important changes)

* Added a new context processor (`inject_class_context`) in `app/__init__.py` to inject the current class context and a list of available classes for student navigation. This supports multi-tenancy and enables dynamic class switching.
* Implemented a new route `switch_class` in `app/routes/student.py` to handle switching between classes using a `join_code`, updating the session and returning relevant class information. The old `switch_period` route is now deprecated. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c31fad6206ab0cc95afca200006187d3a1c53959b7e400aab21d648ce522a855R2494-R2533) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c31fad6206ab0cc95afca200006187d3a1c53959b7e400aab21d648ce522a855L2499-R2542)

### UI enhancements for class switching

* Added a class switcher dropdown to both desktop (`templates/layout_student.html`) and mobile (`templates/mobile/layout_student.html`) layouts, displaying available classes and allowing students to switch context via the UI. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5f72ce29f4faa69602b0538f33a8ff6e88a0905a876da93cc6b8de141674b1dcR479-R526) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-033c19e6fe76b937f41e03d41e64bf4ed02439f27304e1e6bb2a081c6b3053e8R82-R116)
* Implemented client-side JavaScript in both layouts to handle class switching via AJAX, updating the UI and reloading the page on successful switch. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5f72ce29f4faa69602b0538f33a8ff6e88a0905a876da93cc6b8de141674b1dcR688-R730) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-033c19e6fe76b937f41e03d41e64bf4ed02439f27304e1e6bb2a081c6b3053e8R161-R203)
* Improved mobile layout styling for class context display and ensured CSRF tokens are included for secure requests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-033c19e6fe76b937f41e03d41e64bf4ed02439f27304e1e6bb2a081c6b3053e8R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-033c19e6fe76b937f41e03d41e64bf4ed02439f27304e1e6bb2a081c6b3053e8R37-R41)

### Account balance scoping

* Fixed account balance calculations in `app/routes/student.py` to properly scope both checking and savings balances by `join_code`, ensuring students see accurate balances for the selected class. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c31fad6206ab0cc95afca200006187d3a1c53959b7e400aab21d648ce522a855L1163-R1169) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c31fad6206ab0cc95afca200006187d3a1c53959b7e400aab21d648ce522a855R1197-R1198)
* Updated account balance rendering in both desktop and mobile transfer templates to use the new scoped balances, reflecting the correct values for the selected class context. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-992cb241cad91cfccdf749f1749710bbe19fcb40c685a2efdf3cf3bb3294ec73L16-R20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f23e8fe095bd4d9be888ff2907bb3255be0f91304b4eb575a37850692f9e5107L44-R58) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f23e8fe095bd4d9be888ff2907bb3255be0f91304b4eb575a37850692f9e5107L140-R146)

author: copilot
body:
Addresses review feedback on PR #25 requesting confirmation that `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` is correct for PowerShell 7.4 in Azure Functions/Automation context.

## Findings

In PowerShell 7.4, `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` does **not** add a BOM (Byte Order Mark). This is a breaking change from PowerShell 5.1 where it would add a BOM.

Verified behavior:
- `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` → First bytes: `3C 3F 78` (XML start, no BOM) ✓
- Both `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText()` with `UTF8Encoding($false)` produce identical results in PS 7.4

## Conclusion

Current code at line 234 in `Prosjektdokumentgenerering/run.ps1` is correct:
```powershell
Set-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Value $content -Encoding UTF8
```

No changes required. PPTX XML files will not be corrupted by BOM in PowerShell 7.4+ environments.

body:
## Summary

Integrates the TRMNL Categories API (`/api/categories`) into the Android app, providing the foundation for category-based recipe filtering.

## Changes

### API Layer (`api` module)

- **CategoriesResponse Model**: New data class with 27 available plugin categories
  ```kotlin
  @Serializable
  data class CategoriesResponse(
      @SerialName("data")
      val data: List<String>
  )
  ```

- **TrmnlApiService**: Added `getCategories()` endpoint
  - No authentication required
  - Returns `ApiResult<CategoriesResponse, ApiError>`
  - Comprehensive KDoc with usage examples

- **TrmnlDeviceRepository**: Added `getCategories()` method
  - Uses `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` for background execution
  - Returns unwrapped `List<String>` from response
  - Type-safe error handling with EitherNet's `ApiResult`

### Testing

- **TrmnlCategoriesApiTest**: Comprehensive unit tests
  - Tests successful response with all 27 categories
  - Tests HTTP error handling (404, 500)
  - Tests empty category list
  - Uses existing `categories.json` test resource
  - All assertions use AssertK (not JUnit)

- **Updated Test Fakes**: Added `getCategories()` to all FakeApiService implementations:
  - `TrmnlDevicesScreenTest`
  - `DeviceCatalogPresenterTest`
  - `DevicePreviewScreenTest`
  - `RecipesRepositoryTest`
  - `FakeTrmnlApiService`

### Documentation

- **CHANGELOG.md**: Added entry under `[Unreleased] > ### Added`
- **API Documentation**: Inline KDoc with examples for all new methods

## Categories Available

The API returns 27 plugin categories:
analytics, art, calendar, comics, crm, custom, discovery, ecommerce, education, email, entertainment, environment, finance, games, humor, images, kpi, life, marketing, nature, news, personal, productivity, programming, sales, sports, travel

## Testing

✅ All tests pass:
```bash
./gradlew test
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 18s
```

✅ Code formatted:
```bash
./gradlew formatKotlin
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 4s
```

## Usage Example

```kotlin
val repository = TrmnlDeviceRepository(apiService, "user_abc123")

when (val result = repository.getCategories()) {
    is ApiResult.Success -> {
        println("Available categories: ${result.value.joinToString(", ")}")
    }
    is ApiResult.Failure.HttpFailure -> {
        println("HTTP Error: ${result.code}")
    }
    is ApiResult.Failure.NetworkFailure -> {
        println("Network Error")
    }
    // ... other failure types
}
```

## Related Issues

Closes #383

**Blocks**: #384 (Recipe filtering by category)

## Checklist

- [x] API endpoint added to `TrmnlApiService`
- [x] Data models created (`CategoriesResponse`)
- [x] Repository method implemented
- [x] Unit tests written (with AssertK)
- [x] Error handling validated
- [x] All test fakes updated
- [x] Code formatted with `./gradlew formatKotlin`
- [x] All tests pass `./gradlew test`
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated

---

This PR provides the foundation for Issue #384 (category-based recipe filtering). Once merged, the categories can be used to implement filtering in the `RecipesCatalogScreen`.

body:
Implements complete AArch64 assembly generation API matching the existing x86-64 architecture, plus full translation implementation for mapping x86-64 instructions to AArch64 with label-based stack-based calling convention and AArch64 System V ABI-compliant register mapping.

## Architecture

**Core types** (`lib.rs`):
- `AArch64Arch` config, 16 condition codes, register class enum
- 31 GPRs (X0-X30) + SP, 32 SIMD (V0-V31) with element qualifiers

**Instruction system** (`out.rs`):
- `WriterCore` trait: 27+ instructions (MOV, ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, branches, MRS NZCV, MSR NZCV, etc.)
- `Writer<L>` trait: label support with `b_label` and `bl_label` methods for branch-to-label operations
- Memory addressing: `[base, #disp]`, `[base, offset, LSL #scale]`
- **3-operand ADD/SUB**: Uses proper AArch64 semantics `add dest, src1, src2` instead of 2-operand in-place modification

**Output generation** (`out/asm.rs`):
- Macro-based text emission for all instructions
- MOVZ/MOVK sequences for 64-bit immediates
- Label-based branching support
- System register access (MRS/MSR for NZCV flags)

## x86-64 Translation Shim

Full implementation in `shim/mod.rs` for translating x86-64 to AArch64:

**MemArg Adapter Layer**:
- `MemArgAdapter`: Converts x86-64 MemArg trait objects to AArch64 MemArg trait objects
- Handles register arguments, literals, and memory references
- Converts displacement types (u32 → i32)
- Maps register classes (Xmm → Simd, Gpr → Gpr)

**X64ToAArch64Shim**:
- Fully implements x86-64 `WriterCore` and `Writer<L>` traits
- Requires `Writer<ShimLabel>` for CALL shim implementation
- Automatic argument conversion via `MemArgAdapter`
- All 25+ instructions translated with proper semantics
- **Comprehensive memory operand handling**: All instructions support memory operands with automatic LDR/STR insertion

**AArch64 System V ABI Register Mapping**:
- RAX (0) → X0 (0) - argument/return register
- RCX (1) → X1 (1) - argument register
- RDX (2) → X2 (2) - argument register
- RBX (3) → X19 (19) - **callee-saved register**
- RSP (4) → SP (31) - stack pointer
- RBP (5) → X29 (29) - **frame pointer**
- RSI (6) → X3 (3) - argument register
- RDI (7) → X4 (4) - argument register
- R8-R15 → X5-X12, X20-X28

**WriterShimExt Extension Trait**:
- Helper methods on `Writer<ShimLabel>` for memory operations
- `load_to_reg`: Automatically LDR if source is memory, MOV otherwise
- `store_from_reg`: Automatically STR if dest is memory, MOV otherwise

**Label-Based Stack-Based Calling Convention**:
- `ShimLabel` newtype over `usize` for shim label management (formatted as `.Lshim_{N}`)
- **CALL instructions**: Uses label-based shims that push LR and branch to target (7 AArch64 instructions)
  - Jumps over shim label
  - Emits shim code (push LR, branch to target)
  - Sets skip label
  - Branch-and-links to shim label
- **RET instructions**: Directly emit inline code that pops return address from stack into LR, then returns (3 instructions)
- Maintains x86-64 semantics where return addresses live on the stack rather than in LR register
- More efficient on AArch64 CPUs by using proper shim functions

**Direct mappings** (1:1 with memory operand support):
- MOV, ADD, SUB, CMP, AND, OR, XOR, SHL, SHR, MUL, DIV, IDIV, JMP

**Complex translations** (multi-instruction):
- XCHG → 3× MOV (non-atomic)
- PUSH/POP → 2× instructions (SUB+STR / LDR+ADD)
- PUSHF/POPF → 3× instructions (MRS NZCV+SUB+STR / LDR+ADD+MSR NZCV)
- CALL → 7× instructions (label-based shim: B+label+SUB+STR+B+skip+BL)
- RET → 3× instructions (LDR+ADD+RET)
- Memory operands in arithmetic/logical ops → LDR/operation/STR sequences

**Approximations**:
- Parity flags → always true (no AArch64 equivalent)

Condition code translation table maps x86-64 flags (E, NE, B, A, L, G, etc.) to AArch64 (EQ, NE, LO, HI, LT, GT, etc.).

## Examples

### Direct AArch64 Usage
```rust
use portal_solutions_asm_aarch64::{AArch64Arch, out::{Writer, WriterCore}};

let cfg = AArch64Arch::default();
let mut output = String::new();

// Generate AArch64 assembly (3-operand form)
WriterCore::mov(&mut output, cfg, &x0, &x1)?;
WriterCore::add(&mut output, cfg, &x0, &x0, &imm)?;  // dest = src1 + src2
WriterCore::mrs_nzcv(&mut output, cfg, &x0)?;         // Read NZCV flags
Writer::bl_label(&mut output, cfg, label)?;           // Branch with link to label
WriterCore::ret(&mut output, cfg)?;
```

### x86-64 to AArch64 Translation with Stack-Based Calling Convention
```rust
use portal_solutions_asm_x86_64::{X64Arch, out::WriterCore as X64WriterCore};
use portal_solutions_asm_aarch64::shim::X64ToAArch64Shim;

let mut output = String::new();
let writer: &mut dyn Write = &mut output;
let mut shim = X64ToAArch64Shim::new(writer);

// Use x86-64 instruction API, get AArch64 output with ABI-compliant mapping
X64WriterCore::mov(&mut shim, cfg, &dest, &src)?;     // Handles memory operands
X64WriterCore::add(&mut shim, cfg, &dest, &src)?;     // Automatic LDR/STR
X64WriterCore::call(&mut shim, cfg, &target)?;        // Label-based shim handles stack
X64WriterCore::ret(&mut shim, cfg)?;                  // Pops from stack
```

Translation examples:
```rust
// x86-64: PUSH rax
// AArch64:
sub sp, sp, #8
str x0, [sp]

// x86-64: CALL target
// AArch64 (label-based shim):
b .Lskip_0              // Jump over shim
.Lshim_0:               // Shim label
  sub sp, sp, #8
  str x30, [sp]         // Push LR
  b target              // Branch to target
.Lskip_0:               // Skip label
  bl .Lshim_0           // Call shim

// x86-64: RET
// AArch64 (inline):
ldr x30, [sp]           // Pop return address
add sp, sp, #8
ret

// x86-64: ADD rax, [rbx]  (memory source)
// AArch64:
ldr x16, [x19]          // Load from memory (RBX→X19 per ABI)
add x0, x0, x16         // Add to RAX (RAX→X0 per ABI, 3-operand)

// x86-64: MOV [rsi], rdx  (memory dest)
// AArch64:
str x2, [x3]            // Store to memory (RDX→X2, RSI→X3 per ABI)

// x86-64: PUSHF
// AArch64:
mrs x16, nzcv           // Read NZCV flags
sub sp, sp, #8
str x16, [sp]           // Push flags

// x86-64: POPF
// AArch64:
ldr x16, [sp]           // Pop flags
add sp, sp, #8
msr nzcv, x16           // Write NZCV flags

// x86-64: XCHG rax, rbx
// AArch64:
mov x16, x0
mov x0, x19             // RBX→X19 per ABI (callee-saved)
mov x19, x16
```

## Testing

- 5 passing tests including shim tests
- Tests for MemArg adapter conversion
- Tests for basic shim operations (HLT, RET, CALL)
- All builds successful with no security issues

Then create a "shim" in the `shim` directory in that crate which translates x86_64 assembly to aarch64 assembly (implementing the x86_64 traits on a wrapper over the new aarch64 traits), adding needed constructs in aarch64 as you go. Don't worry about perfect accuracy, but make sure the aarch64 output functions identically in most cases to the x86_64 one--document any "skips" you make for performance.

author: rallinator7
body:
## Summary

When a user creates an organization, they are now automatically connected to that organization via a new `user_organizations` join table. The entire operation happens atomically within a database transaction.

### Changes
- **Database**: Added `user_organizations` join table with composite primary key `(user_id, organization_id)` and appropriate foreign keys/indexes
- **Domain Layer**: Updated `CreateOrganizationInput` to require mandatory `user_id`
- **Repository Layer**: `PostgresOrganizationRepository.create_organization()` now uses a transaction to insert both the organization and user-organization link atomically
- **gRPC Layer**: `OrganizationServiceHandler` now extracts `user_id` from the `authorization` header JWT token - authentication is **mandatory** for organization creation
- **Test Script**: Updated `scripts/test-grpc-api.sh` to register/login a user and pass JWT token when creating organizations

### Key Implementation Details
- Transaction logic is contained entirely in the PostgreSQL layer - domain layer remains unaware of transactions
- Added `UserOrganizationAlreadyExists` error for duplicate link detection
- Foreign key violations (user doesn't exist) return `UserNotFound` error
- Unauthenticated requests to `CreateOrganization` now return `UNAUTHENTICATED` status

Closes #76

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests pass: `cargo test --workspace --lib`
- [x] Build succeeds: `cargo build -p ponix-all-in-one`
- [x] Start services and run `scripts/test-grpc-api.sh`
- [x] Verify `user_organizations` table contains link: `docker exec -it ponix-postgres psql -U ponix -d ponix -c "SELECT * FROM user_organizations;"`
- [x] Verify unauthenticated org creation is rejected

1. Basic monitoring (WebSocket + REST API with rate limit protection)
2. Consciousness integration (ThoughtStream, AutonomousWondering, KnowledgeBase)
3. Strategic decision-making (dynamic fee estimation, mining pool tracking)
4. Advanced features (Lightning Network, transaction acceleration, multi-network support)

**Required for operation**: Single API key from mempool.space (free tier sufficient with proper rate limiting)

**Documentation structure**:
- `BITCOIN_MEMPOOL_INTEGRATION_COMPLETE.md` - Primary integration guide (29KB)
- `BITCOIN_MINING_LIGHTNING_INTELLIGENCE.md` - Mining/Lightning analytics (31KB)
- `MEMPOOL_API_REFERENCE.md` - Complete API documentation (28KB)
- `MEMPOOL_LIGHTNING_NODE_CONNECTION.md` - Node connection guide (14KB)
- `BITCOIN_MEMPOOL_SESSION_SUMMARY.md` - Session summary (14KB)
- `MEMPOOL_RATE_LIMITING_CRITICAL.md` - Critical rate limit protection guide (14KB)
- `MEMPOOL_SELF_HOSTED_GUIDE.md` - Self-hosted deployment guide (14KB)
- **`BITCOIN_EXTENDED_NETWORKS.md`** - **NEW**: Extended networks guide (13KB)
- `.env.example` - **UPDATED**: Rate limit warnings and safe defaults

**Rate Limiting Configuration** (CRITICAL):
- Default polling interval: 60 seconds (safe for public API)
- WebSocket primary method: Unlimited real-time updates
- REST fallback only: Minimal periodic calls
- Rate limit tracking: Built-in monitoring code
- Emergency procedures: Ban recovery documented

**Self-Hosted Discovery**:
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/mempool/mempool (entire stack is open source!)
- **Cost**: $25-50/month (vs $100+ enterprise sponsorship)
- **Benefit**: NO rate limits (unlimited API access)
- **Performance**: 10-second polling possible (6x better than public API)
- **Control**: Full customization and private deployment

**Extended Networks** (NEW):
- **Liquid Network**: https://liquid.network/ - Bitcoin sidechain with 2-minute blocks, confidential transactions
- **Mempool.space Liquid**: Full API support at https://liquid.network/api/v1
- **Use cases**: Exchange arbitrage (faster settlement), privacy-sensitive transactions, asset issuance
- **Mining Pool APIs**: Direct integration with ViaBTC, F2Pool, AntPool, Binance Pool
- **Private relay**: Submit high-value transactions directly to pools (MEV protection)
- **Multi-network strategy**: Optimal network selection based on speed/privacy/cost requirements

**Strategic window**: Current low-fee environment (3.2 sat/vB) provides 2-year opportunity before halving increases competition 2-3x.

Related to previous Bitcoin mempool autonomous study (Dec 3, 2025) documented in `MEMPOOL_STUDY_COMPLETE.md`.

body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive context engineering system based on Google's research and Claude Skills patterns.

### What's Included

**Phase 1: Session Management**
- Persistent session state across conversations
- Tracks active files, pending tasks, decisions, and context
- Auto-save on changes with session archiving
- Target: <100ms load time

**Phase 2: Memory System**
- Declarative/procedural/episodic memory types
- Provenance tracking (source, timestamp, confidence)
- Confidence decay for inferred memories
- Search, access tracking, and auto-archiving

**Phase 3: Progressive Disclosure**
- 3-tier skill loading (metadata → instructions → resources)
- Tier 1: ~50 tokens, Tier 2: ~500 tokens, Tier 3: ~2000+ tokens
- Achieves ~90% token reduction vs. loading all resources

**Context Retrieval Engine**
- Intelligent context assembly with push/pull patterns
- Combines sessions, memories, and skills
- Token estimation and optimization

**New /context Command**
- Session management (status, archive)
- Memory operations (remember, search, export)
- Task tracking (add, list, complete)
- Decision recording
- Context summary generation

### Files Added

- `src/context/types.ts` - Type definitions (150 lines)
- `src/context/session.ts` - Session management (300 lines)
- `src/context/memory.ts` - Memory system (350 lines)
- `src/context/progressive.ts` - Progressive disclosure (250 lines)
- `src/context/retrieval.ts` - Context assembly (200 lines)
- `src/context/index.ts` - Main exports
- `content/commands/context.md` - /context command documentation
- `plans/context-engineering-implementation.md` - Implementation plan

### Validation

✅ All TypeScript files compile successfully  
✅ Build passes (119ms)  
✅ 15 commands available (including new /context)  
✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality  
✅ .gitignore updated for .ferg-context/ local storage

### Research Foundation

- [Google Context Engineering](https://www.news.aakashg.com/p/context-engineering) - Aakash Gupta
- [Claude Skills Deep Dive](https://rickhightower.substack.com/p/claude-skills-deep-dive) - Rick Hightower
- [Principled Instructions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.16171) - MBZUAI

### Next Steps

- Phase 4: Context Retrieval optimization
- Phase 5: Agent integration
- Phase 6: Production polish and performance tuning

author: covulor-stage[bot]
body:
I replaced the vulnerable string-built SQL with a parameterized query and passed user inputs as parameters to cursor.execute. Instead of concatenating username and password directly into the SQL string (which allowed injection like "admin'; DROP TABLE users; --"), the code now uses sqlite3 qmark-style parameters: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password = ?" and cursor.execute(query, (username, password)). This prevents user input from being interpreted as SQL syntax and mitigates SQL injection.

Additional tips and considerations:
- Use secure password storage: never store plaintext passwords; store salted password hashes (e.g., bcrypt, Argon2) and verify with a hashing function rather than querying by password.
- Use context managers for connections/cursors (with sqlite3.connect(db_file) as conn:) to ensure proper cleanup on errors.
- Prefer higher-level ORMs or query builders that use parameterization by default (e.g., SQLAlchemy with bound parameters) for more complex queries.
- Limit database privileges for the connection user to reduce impact of any compromise.
- Avoid logging sensitive values (like raw passwords) and validate user input where appropriate.

This change directly addresses the identified weakness by removing raw SQL construction with untrusted input and using prepared/parameterized statements so the DB treats inputs as data, not executable SQL.

### Diagnostic Logging for Missing Audio Segments

Added `log_event()` function and logging throughout the audio pipeline:

| Event Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `[EVENT:SILENT]` | Audio segment detected as silent (includes RMS stats and reason) |
| `[EVENT:QUEUE_BACKLOG]` | Queue has >10 segments pending (warning, not dropped) |
| `[EVENT:VLC_PAUSE]` | VLC detected playing, recording paused |

| `[EVENT:CLEAN_FAIL]` | Sox audio cleaning failed |
| `[EVENT:NO_TRANSCRIPT]` | Transcription returned empty result |
| `[EVENT:ERROR]` | Processing or main loop exception |

author: pciolkosz
body:
`cudaGetDriverEntryPoint` will always request the version of a function that matches the current CUDA Runtime version. This is not minor version compatibility friendly and older driver will just respond with invalid value error.

We made a switch to use `cudaGetDriverEntryPoint` in order to fix https://github.com/NVIDIA/cccl/issues/5970, but that broke minor version compatibility. This PR brings back `cudaGetDriverEntryPointByVersion` at least for CUDA 13.X CTK.

There will probably need to be a follow-up change to instead switch to dlopen + dlsym in order to fix this in 12.X

Spring Boot 4 automatically creates a DataSource for Flyway when `spring.flyway.url` or `spring.flyway.user` is set. The manual `@FlywayDataSource` bean configuration is no longer necessary.

- Integration tests used `spring.datasource.*` properties

**After:**
- Flyway auto-configuration creates DataSource from `spring.flyway.url/user/password`
- Integration tests use `spring.flyway.*` properties

author: copilot
body:
SonarCloud Windows workflow fails because it uses Ninja+MinGW, not MSVC. The CMakeLists.txt `if(MSVC)` block doesn't match MinGW builds, causing them to fall through to the Linux `else()` block which unconditionally links X11::X11.

### Changes

- **X11 linking**: Move from main link list to conditional `if(UNIX AND NOT APPLE)` block
- **DbgHelp**: Make optional (`QUIET`) for non-MSVC Windows compilers since FindDbgHelp.cmake only auto-detects with MSVC
- **MinGW Windows support**: Add platform-specific libraries when `WIN32` detected in else block:
  - `winmm` for multimedia functions
  - Optional `DbgHelp` when found
  - Windows version defines for C++20 compatibility

```cmake
# X11 is only available and needed on Unix/Linux systems (not Windows/macOS)
if(UNIX AND NOT APPLE)
  target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE X11::X11)
endif()

# Windows-specific libraries when building with MinGW/GCC instead of MSVC
if(WIN32)
  target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE winmm)
  if(DBGHELP_FOUND)
    target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE ${DBGHELP_LIBRARY})
  endif()
endif()
```

author: carlosmsanchezm
body:
## Summary
Extends the observability platform with a complete logging solution using Loki for log storage and Fluent Bit for log shipping. The logging stack runs alongside the existing metrics stack (Prometheus + metrics-server) in a dedicated namespace.

## Changes
- **Logging Infrastructure**: Loki single-binary deployment with 7-day retention and filesystem storage
- **Log Collection**: Fluent Bit DaemonSet collecting container logs and Kubernetes events
- **Structured Labels**: Logs tagged with cluster, namespace, pod, container, app, event reason/type
- **Configuration**: New Helm value files for Loki (`loki-values.yaml`) and Fluent Bit (`fluent-bit-values.yaml`)
- **API Extensions**: Updated CRD and Go types to export Loki service endpoints via `ProjectInfra.status.outputs[].observability`
- **Documentation**: Enhanced OBSERVABILITY.md with logging architecture, query contract, and validation steps

## Technical Details
- **Namespace**: `aegis-logging` (separate from metrics namespace)
- **Storage**: Filesystem-based (non-persistent) with 7d retention
- **Log Shipping**: Container logs + K8s events via Fluent Bit DaemonSet
- **Query Interface**: Backend can proxy log queries via exported `lokiService`/`lokiPort` outputs
- **Security**: ClusterIP services only, no public exposure

## Backend Integration
The logging stack exports these new fields in observability outputs:
- `lokiNamespace`: Namespace where Loki runs (`aegis-logging`)
- `lokiService`: Loki service name
- `lokiPort`: Loki HTTP port (3100)
- `lokiAuthSecret`: Auth secret name (empty when auth disabled)

Backend can build in-cluster URLs as: `http://<lokiService>.<lokiNamespace>.svc:<lokiPort>`

## Files Changed
- 9 files modified, 711 insertions(+), 26 deletions(-)
- New: `fluent-bit-values.yaml`, `loki-values.yaml`
- Updated: CRDs, API types, stack installer, documentation

## Testing
Validated on both local (docker-desktop) and AWS EKS clusters. See OBSERVABILITY.md for validation steps.

body: Polymarket emits an OrderFilled event for both sides of every trade - one reflecting the maker’s perspective and one reflecting the taker’s. If we sum these events directly, every trade is counted twice. Dividing the total by 2 converts this into a correct one-sided volume that reflects the actual economic size of trades. This adjustment is also important for swaps and merge/split operations: in these cases the maker and taker may have different asset movements or token amounts, but they still represent a single matched trade. Without dividing by 2, these complex fills would artificially inflate volume. By normalizing this way, we ensure consistent, accurate volume reporting across all trade types

## Overview

Implements comprehensive safety features for the artifact audit tool to prevent PR #6 disaster (metadata corruption, date overwriting, archive violations).

## Key Features

### 🛡️ Smart Date Inference
- **4-stage fallback**: Git creation date → Git last modified → Filesystem mtime → Present date
- Prevents date overwriting (PR #6 issue where all dates became present date)
- Preserves historical context from git history

### 📂 Directory Exclusion
- **Protected by default**: `archive/`, `deprecated/`, `vlm_reports/`
- Configurable via `.agentqms/settings.yaml`
- Override available with `--include-excluded` flag

### ✅ Pre-flight Safety
- Preview changes before applying (grouped by directory)
- Confirmation prompt (bypass with `--no-confirm` for automation)
- Automatic git stash backup before changes (bypass with `--no-stash` for CI)

### 🎯 VLM Report Standardization
- New `vlm_report` artifact type (not `BUG` prefix)
- Migration tool for batch renaming
- Proper frontmatter: `type: vlm_report`, `category: evaluation`

## Implementation

### Core Tools
- `AgentQMS/agent_tools/audit/artifact_audit.py` (23 KB) - Enhanced audit tool with safety features
- `AgentQMS/agent_tools/utilities/migrate_vlm_reports.py` (4.5 KB) - VLM migration utility

### Configuration
- `AgentQMS/knowledge/agent/artifact_rules.yaml` - Added `vlm_report` type definition

- `AgentQMS/interface/Makefile` - 8 new safe-by-default audit targets

### Documentation
- `AgentQMS/knowledge/agent/artifact-audit-improvements.md` (361 lines) - Comprehensive usage guide

## Execution Results

✅ **79 artifacts processed** successfully  
✅ **51 artifacts properly excluded** (archive/, deprecated/, vlm_reports/)  
✅ **44 artifacts updated** with missing/incomplete frontmatter  
✅ **2 VLM reports migrated** to `vlm_report_` standard  

## Testing

All features tested and validated:
- ✅ Smart date inference extracts correct KST timestamps from git history
- ✅ Directory exclusion correctly filters protected directories
- ✅ Pre-flight preview shows grouped changes by directory
- ✅ VLM migration renames files and updates frontmatter correctly
- ✅ Makefile targets all functional and discoverable

## Commits

- `e261cb8` feat(audit): Added Artifact Audit tool safety features for date inference
- `21567ae` feat(agentqms): run artifact audit and add missing frontmatter

Total: 6 commits with audit tool improvements

## Documentation

- Quick start workflows

- Configuration options

- Examples

## How This Prevents PR #6 Disaster
